## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q030](#S04-Q030)

<p>What problems do transactional outbox and inbox patterns address? Trace a business update, an outgoing event and a receiving consumer across their failure boundaries.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Explain and verify the local transaction guarantee while exposing the remaining remote-effect failure boundary.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace business state and outgoing-event records around local commit.</li>
<li>Explain dispatcher retry and repeated publication or delivery.</li>
<li>Identify receiver or external-effect recovery responsibilities.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Protect one intended effect across repeated attempts](messaging-idempotent-consumer.md)

<p>The sender and receiver solve related coordination problems at separate local boundaries. Follow the sender&#x27;s durable change through dispatch to the receiver, then introduce a failure between those stages. That trace distinguishes protected local state from remote effects still needing their own strategy.</p>

### S04-Q030 · Mechanism

<p>What problems do transactional outbox and inbox patterns address? Trace a business update, an outgoing event and a receiving consumer across their failure boundaries.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q030](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q030)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q030](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q030)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain transactional outbox/inbox patterns.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>The question concerns coordination between durable business state and messages. Explain the sender and receiver responsibilities without assuming one transaction spans the entire system.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about local atomicity and remote delivery boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State which records share a database transaction and which effects occur remotely. Verify any chosen database or broker guarantees separately.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace interruption before and after local commit on both sides.</li>
<li>Explain duplicate publication or delivery and a test of the remaining failure window.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming that an outbox alone guarantees every downstream effect happens exactly once.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What must a dispatcher do after an uncertain publish outcome?</li>
<li>How does the design change if the consumer calls an external payment API?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An ASP.NET Core service changes order state in SQL Server and publishes a notification event. The publisher loses the broker response, and the consumer also calls an external email API. Draw the records and states, identify each uncertain outcome and propose evidence for safe recovery without promising one transaction across all participants.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains the purpose of outbox/inbox and names the local transaction scope.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Traces commit, dispatch and receiver failures, qualifies the guarantee and defines validation for remote effects.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A pattern diagram without interruption tests or a separate external-effect contract does not support an end-to-end guarantee.</p>
